t: You're looking at Number 11 Downing Street, the official residence of the Chancellor of the Exchequer. It's a Grade One listed house, and it was built in 1682 alongside Number 10, the Prime Minister's residence next door. The house is credited to Sir Christopher Wren, the architect who was given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the Great Fire of 1666, and who finished St Paul's Cathedral in 1710. So this ordinary-looking terraced house on one of the most famous streets in Britain comes from the same hand as that great dome.
